headline: Good morning — here’s your brief for Wednesday 4 November 2026.

tip.title: Get outside light early in the day
tip.body: Aim for 10 to 15 minutes of outdoor daylight in the first part of your day, such as drinking your coffee on the balcony or walking the last stretch of your commute. Morning light helps keep your body clock steady, which can make it easier to fall asleep at a sensible hour tonight. On a cloudy Melbourne morning, outdoor light is still much brighter than indoor lighting, so it's worth going out anyway.

quote.text: The only way to do great work is to love what you do.
quote.author: Steve Jobs

items.title: Salesforce's Braze deal puts martech consolidation under the spotlight
items.summary: Salesforce agreed on 20 October to buy Braze for about US$5.66 billion, and a new analysis looks at what that means for email service providers, composable CDPs and upcoming renewals. Braze customers could end up renewing with Salesforce whether or not they chose it, so buyers should review their stacks and contracts now.

items.title: Salesforce agrees to buy Cresta, days after the Braze deal
items.summary: A roundup of 2 November martech news lists Salesforce agreeing to acquire Cresta. The roundup doesn't give the price or terms, so treat the details as unconfirmed until Salesforce publishes them, but it adds to a run of Salesforce customer-facing acquisitions.

items.title: New AI features land in asset management and audience tools
items.summary: MarTech's 29 October roundup says Canto added an AI assistant to its asset management platform and Circana launched predictive commerce signals for audiences. It also notes Adobe's partnership with the BWT Alpine Formula One team, which starts in 2027 and uses AI to generate customised fan content.

items.title: EU governments' draft would exempt some ad-measurement cookies from consent
items.summary: A 2 October Council draft of the EU privacy overhaul keeps consent as the default for cookies. It would allow contextual ad measurement and capping cookies without consent, and would shorten the wait before re-asking after a refusal to four months. Ambassadors were expected to vote on it on 11 October, and this is only the Council's opening position ahead of talks with Parliament. I couldn't confirm the vote outcome.

items.title: Gmail now hard-rejects non-compliant bulk email
items.summary: This guide says Gmail has permanently rejected non-compliant bulk mail with 5xx errors since November 2025. Senders of 5,000 or more messages a day to personal accounts need SPF, DKIM and DMARC, one-click unsubscribe, and spam complaints under 0.3%. It's a vendor explainer rather than breaking news, but it's a useful checklist for any email programme.

items.title: Salesforce agrees to buy voice AI firm Cresta
items.summary: Salesforce signed a definitive agreement on 2 November (US time) to acquire Cresta, a voice-first customer experience platform, and plans to fold it into Service Cloud. Salesforce didn't disclose the price, though The Information reportedly put it at about $2.7 billion (unconfirmed). The deal is expected to close in the first quarter of fiscal 2028, and it would give Agentforce a stronger voice channel for contact centres.

items.title: Salesforce closes Listen Labs and Loops deals
items.summary: Salesforce says it completed its purchase of Listen Labs, an AI customer research and simulation platform, on 2 November. It also completed the Loops acquisition on the same day, and Loops' analytics technology is slated to go into Tableau. The two deals add customer-insight and agentic analytics tools to Marketing Cloud, Service Cloud and Tableau.

items.title: Salesforce buys Rune Technologies for national security push
items.summary: Salesforce is acquiring Rune Technologies, which it calls its most significant national security acquisition so far, to bolster its Missionforce government and defence business. Salesforce says that business is growing 80% year on year, and the deal is expected to close in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2027.

items.title: What the Braze deal means for Marketing Cloud users
items.summary: Salesforce Ben looks at what Salesforce's roughly $5.66 billion Braze acquisition means for Marketing Cloud professionals and partners. Salesforce says Braze will be connected with Data 360, Customer 360 and Agentforce, so the main question is how the products will be combined without adding complexity.

items.title: Salesforce adds agent kill switch and cost controls
items.summary: Salesforce has launched an agent kill switch and new cost controls for managing AI agents, as reported by Salesforce Ben on 27 October. It matters for admins watching spend and reliability as agent usage grows and consumption-based pricing comes in.

sfstatus.statusNote: One significant incident hit Marketing Cloud Next on many AU and APAC instances. It was resolved at about 10:29 am AEDT on 3 November. I found no specific planned maintenance for the next 7 days.

items.title: Marketing Cloud Next setup and provisioning blocked on AU/APAC instances, now fixed
items.summary: A feature disruption began at 9:35 pm UTC on 28 October. It stopped Marketing Cloud Growth and Advanced customers from finishing setup or provisioning new orgs, because the Select a Data Space option was missing. Listed instances include AP52, AP53, AP54, AP58, AP60 and the AUS series. Salesforce reverted a configuration change and marked it resolved at 11:29 pm UTC on 2 November, after 5 days and 2 hours. Anyone still affected should check the Known Issue article linked on the incident page.

items.title: Several short Salesforce disruptions logged on 2–3 November, services unspecified
items.summary: This third-party tracker logged feature disruptions on 2 and 3 November. They lasted roughly 1.5 hours and 10 hours, and all were marked resolved. The snippets don't name the affected products or regions, so check Salesforce Trust for your own instance before assuming any impact on Sales/Service Cloud or Data Cloud.

items.title: RBA lifts cash rate to 4.85 per cent in a split vote
items.summary: The Reserve Bank raised the cash rate by 25 basis points to 4.85 per cent on Melbourne Cup Day, its fifth hike this year. Six board members voted for the rise and three wanted to hold, and it is the highest rate since 2008, which adds pressure on mortgage holders.

items.title: Albanese says government will cut spending after rate rise
items.summary: Albanese insisted the government will rein in spending as reaction to the rate hike flowed in. The Coalition says Labor needs to make tough budget decisions, so inflation and spending are set to dominate federal politics.

items.title: Albanese pitches UN Security Council bid at CHOGM in Antigua
items.summary: At the Commonwealth leaders' meeting in Antigua, the prime minister gave a speech backing Australia's bid for a temporary UN Security Council seat from 2029. He spoke about political violence, polarisation and a middle-power push to regulate artificial intelligence.

items.title: Point of Law wins the Melbourne Cup for Ciaron Maher
items.summary: Point of Law, ridden by Ethan Brown, won the 166th Melbourne Cup at Flemington, and trainer Ciaron Maher had the first three placegetters. It capped Victoria's biggest day of racing, which was overshadowed for many households by the same-day rate rise.

items.title: Virgin Australia apologises after breaking girl's $33,000 wheelchair
items.summary: Virgin Australia apologised to a family after a young girl's $33,000 wheelchair was broken on a flight. The ABC lists it as the latest in a run of wheelchair incidents on the airline, and People With Disability Australia calls equipment damage a long-standing issue.

items.title: Cyclone Murasu hits south Andhra Pradesh coast, two dead
items.summary: Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu made landfall near Ongole in Prakasam district in the early hours of Tuesday, and two deaths have been reported in cyclone-related incidents. The NDRF has deployed 14 teams across Andhra Pradesh and named six districts as worst-affected, so relief efforts and damage assessments will continue.

items.title: Sensex climbs more than 1 per cent as rally continues
items.summary: The Sensex was trading around 76,633 at midday on 3 November, up about 1.24 per cent. That is an intraday figure, not the final close, but it points to continued investor confidence in Indian equities.

items.title: Supreme Court says protest sites can't be held indefinitely
items.summary: On 3 November the Supreme Court observed that protest sites cannot be occupied indefinitely and asked the Centre and other parties to respond to a plea. The matter touches on the right to peaceful protest and on traders' livelihoods, and could shape how protests in public spaces such as Jantar Mantar are managed.

items.title: Supreme Court flags open firecracker sales in Delhi, asks Centre to investigate
items.summary: A Supreme Court bench said it was concerned by a newspaper report showing all kinds of firecrackers on open sale in Delhi markets, despite its order the day before, and told the Centre to examine the alleged violations. Only certified green crackers are permitted in Delhi-NCR for now, and the report says a complete ban returns from 9 November.

items.title: India's October factory growth revised lower; rupee steadies
items.summary: Market headlines on this page say India's manufacturing growth for October was revised down, while the rupee rebounded on RBI support. The page gives no further detail, so the size of the revision isn't confirmed here, but it is a sign of softer factory momentum even as equities rally.

items.title: Cyclone Murasu hits coastal Andhra, damaging crops and cutting power
items.summary: Cyclone Murasu crossed the coast near Kothapatnam, close to Ongole. It brought heavy rain and strong winds that disrupted power, flooded roads and damaged crops, with the crop loss put at more than 52,700 hectares (a preliminary figure). The storm was expected to weaken, but more heavy rain is forecast for several districts.

items.title: Naidu says cyclone and El Niño are a combined test as rainfall deficit persists
items.summary: At a review meeting, Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu said protecting lives and speeding up relief and rehabilitation come before electoral considerations. He told people not to panic over rumours about the Budameru stream, and said the state still has a 27 per cent rainfall deficit.

items.title: TDP-led alliance wins Pulivendula, Jagan's home municipality
items.summary: The NDA alliance won 37 of the 40 wards in Pulivendula municipality, and the TDP's candidate won the chairperson post by a large margin. This is a symbolic blow to the YSRCP in its leader's home area, and the alliance also did well across Kadapa district.

items.title: Amaravati officials told to keep floodwater moving after Murasu inflows
items.summary: The head of the Amaravati Development Corporation inspected the streams that run through the capital region and ordered officials to keep floodwater flowing through the designated channels. Around 180 cusecs reaching Undavalli was being pumped into the Krishna River, and the aim is to prevent waterlogging in low-lying areas of the capital.

items.title: Vizag gears up for CII Partnership Summit on 12–13 November
items.summary: Visakhapatnam will host the state's flagship investment summit on 12–13 November, preceded by five regional investment conferences. The government has set up a Group of Ministers and committees, and it will track the MoUs signed (this article is from 5 August, so it is not fresh news, but the event is only days away).
